knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Unapproved products may not match the safety data or dilution rules. The worker stops, does not use the product, and the supervisor decides.
The machine and the socket are switched off before the plug is removed at the plug body. Removing a live plug or pulling by the cord are both unsafe.
Taping or using a damaged cord is unsafe. The worker sets the machine aside, labels it and reports it; repair is not the worker's task.

practicalCriteria: Checks the job record for approved products and required PPE before opening any container, observed by the assessor.
Moves a plug-in machine to another socket using the switch-off sequence (machine, socket, then plug at the plug body), observed by the assessor.
Sets aside and labels a simulated defective machine, reports it, and does not attempt a repair.
Completes an incident or hazard report for a simulated near miss, with time, location and the manager notified.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark, so all three must be correct. Practical competence: assessor sign-off against each practical criterion, observed on site or in a simulated setting. A knowledge-check pass does not verify practical competence. Reporting timeframe: set by the business.
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation sheet for the switch-off sequence and the defective-equipment step
Completed simulated incident or hazard report
stopWorkCriteria: A machine with a cut or damaged cord is used
The worker attempts an electrical repair
An unapproved product is used or mixed
